peg.volatility_score_basis: CUT 6.5 -> 5.5 on 2026-10-04, AND NOT BECAUSE ANYTHING DETERIORATED -- every figure that justified the 6.5 improved and the row was still wrong. The 2026-09-14 note deferred this re-rate and named its conditions ('STRC concentration and the exit asymmetry, both unchanged'); ONE OF THOSE PREMISES IS FALSE. RESOLVED: '~-9% below NAV' -> -1.34% (nav_spread_pct); 'NAV ~1.376' -> 1.436830, strictly monotonic across 722 readings with zero drawdown; 'underlying undercollateralized ~95%' -> 101.5602%. Accrual is real and rate-consistent at 13.51% 30d / 14.25% 7d against STRC's 11-15% indicated, and the one-way ratchet held through the June event. WHY CUT ANYWAY: THE 6.5 CREDITED NAV SMOOTHNESS THAT IS SUBSTANTIALLY DEFINITIONAL. apyUSD's NAV IS total_assets/shares -- PegTracker flags the same tautology on share_coverage_tautological_pct ('Definitional, not measured ... it carries no information about backing'). Zero drawdown in 722 readings is a property of the formula as much as of the assets. AND THE MARK IS WEAK THREE WAYS: 52.18% of the STRC bucket ($80,169,860) is marked at an UNDISCLOSED issuer price; the verifiable 47.82% is marked off a venue holding ~$371K against a $70.8M position; and THIS EXACT NAV HAS ALREADY BEEN INFLATED ONCE FROM THIS EXACT SOURCE -- the June post-mortem records that Apyx's own dashboard showed an inflated NAV from a STRCx pricing bug. Precedented, not hypothetical. AND THE ONLY INDEPENDENT PRICE SIGNAL HAS NEVER AGREED WITH THE NAV: 0 of 722 readings at or above it on the DEX measure, 0 of 702 on CoinGecko. TWO FIELDS BOTH LABELLED discount-to-NAV DIFFER BY ~190BPS ON THE 30-DAY MEAN (-1.674% DEX vs -3.58% CoinGecko); THE DEX MEASURE BINDS because that is where a holder transacts, and the 2026-09-29 FIRED alert at -1.38% is that measure -- now -1.336%, essentially unchanged, NOT recovered. Second false premise: capture is 55.24%, not 'roughly a third'. NOT cut further because the accrual, rate consistency and ratchet are genuinely verified.

liquidity.liquidity_score_basis: HELD at 3.5 on 2026-10-04. REDEMPTION IS NOW FOLDED INTO THIS AXIS PER SPEC and the fold is numerically a no-op: the legacy redemption_score was 3.5 against this 3.5, so the worse link was already here. The fold DID remove a seventh term from a six-axis mean -- the checker was dividing by 7, understating the mean and therefore every above-mean gap on this report. MEASURED: derived score 3.5 (status computed), TVL $16,626,428. DEPTH IS CENSORED, NOT MEASURED -- total_2pct_depth reports $100,000 with is_floor true and status ladder_exhausted, so the crossing is above where we look and a floor may not lift a score. THE COOLDOWN IS KNOWN RATHER THAN ASSUMED, the one place this asset is better documented than its parent: cooldown_days 20.0 with duration_known true AND duration_documented_days 20.0 -- measured and documented AGREE. AND THE QUEUE IS EFFECTIVELY EMPTY: queue_depth_apxusd 194.51 on a $167M asset, week_over_week_growth_x 1.0. THAT IS NOT PRICED AS COMFORT AND THE AMBIGUITY IS THE POINT -- an empty exit queue is equally consistent with holders being content and with the claim being unattractive to exit at a 1.34% discount to a NAV they cannot realise for 20 days. drain_rate_7d and implied_wait_days are both NULL, so the queue has never drained enough to measure a wait: the 20 days is a DOCUMENTED duration, not an OBSERVED one. Held at 3.5 and not above because the two exits fail together: the DEX two-hop runs through apxUSD's own thin book and the primary route through apxUSD's gated off-chain RFQ. A wrapper's exit cannot beat its underlying's, and apxUSD's is 3.5.

overall.overall_score_basis: RAISED 3.0 -> 4.0 on 2026-10-04 by owner ruling, against my recommendation of 3.5. Sits 0.0833 BELOW the axis mean of 4.0833, so the at-or-below convention is satisfied and NO spec section-4 disclosure or OVERALL_EXEMPT registration is owed. THE OWNER'S QUESTION IS WHAT PRODUCED THE AXIS-1 CUT AND IT IS THE REUSABLE PART OF THIS PASS: asked why I was placing overall 0.75 BELOW the mean, the answer turned out to be that the MEAN was wrong, not the overall. Axis 1 at 6.5 carried the gap single-handed -- the other five averaged 3.80 -- and it credited NAV smoothness that is definitional. Cutting it to 5.5 moved the mean 4.25 -> 4.0833 and the gap 0.75 -> 0.0833. A LARGE BELOW-MEAN GAP IS A SIGNAL TO AUDIT THE AXES, NOT A PLACEMENT TO DEFEND. WHY 4.0 RATHER THAN PARITY WITH apxUSD's 3.5: axes 2, 4, 5 and 6 are IDENTICAL between the two (same reserve, same three Safes, same issuer) and axis 3 is equal at 3.5. The pair differs on exactly one axis and the 0.5 overall gap tracks the 2.0 axis-1 gap, damped. apxUSD promises $1 and misses by 1.10%; apyUSD promises NAV and never promised immediate parity, so its 1.34% discount is a time-value and liquidity charge on a 20-day claim, not a failed peg. And apyUSD strictly dominates: it takes all the yield AND exits first. A PURE WRAPPER SCORING ABOVE ITS UNDERLYING DESERVES A STATED REASON EVEN THOUGH NOTHING ENFORCES IT -- the PURE_WRAPPERS guard checks AXIS 4 ONLY (equal at 3.0), so overall is unconstrained by construction. The reason is NOT transferable: it rests on apyUSD making a different PROMISE, not on holding different assets. THE DOMINANCE IS ALSO THE FINDING, NOT PURELY A CREDIT: at 55.24% capture the MAJORITY of supply is the privileged claim, and the 44.76% bearing the uncompensated residual is apxUSD at 3.5. PATH DOWN: apxUSD's Backing re-crossing 100%, or the DEX discount breaching its -4.01% 30-day floor. PATH UP: a NAV mark independent of the issuer -- the single measurement this whole report is missing.
